stories.title: U.S. steps in to prop up Japan's yen for first time in decades
stories.summary: The U.S. has intervened to support Japan's currency after a prolonged slide, a notable break from the hands-off approach Washington has taken toward the yen for decades. The move signals concern in Washington about the pace of the yen's weakening and what it could mean for trade and financial stability.
stories.whyItMatters: A rare U.S. currency intervention on Japan's behalf could reshape FX markets and suggests policymakers now see yen weakness as a systemic risk rather than just a Japan problem.
